To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the exercise programs in the RESOLVE study were safe and feasible and resulted in significant improvements in body composition, cardiovascular disease risk factors, and quality of life.

The RESOLVE randomized controlled trial demonstrated that 6 weeks of exercise, either aerobic (walking), resistance (weight training), or both (combination), reduced visceral fat and improved cardiovascular risk factors in individuals with metabolic syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exercise on the body and mind.
the study of the effects of different modalities of physical activity in metabolic syndrome (MetS), with a particular emphasis on the reduction of visceral fat mass.
the effects of exercise and diet on the body composition of overweight individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are a number of different exercise modalities that can be used to reduce visceral fat, and that these different exercise modalities can reduce the risk for cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.
exercise is an important component of the treatment for metabolic syndrome.
there is no clear evidence that any particular exercise mode or type is superior to any other in terms of reducing visceral fat mass and/or cardiovascular risk in patients with Metabolic Syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that a combination of aerobic exercise and resistance exercise is the best approach for improving insulin resistance, and that the addition of diet is not necessary to achieve the greatest benefit.
exercise is a powerful intervention for reducing cardiovascular disease risk factors in metabolic syndrome.
we found that exercise training, in general, is beneficial in improving metabolic risk factors, including blood pressure, glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, lipid profile and inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

exercise training, especially high intensity interval training, is a safe, effective and time-efficient way to reduce the risk factors associated with metabolic syndrome, which is a cluster of conditions that includes obesity, high blood pressure, high triglycerides and low HDL cholesterol.
exercise can help to reduce visceral fat and improve metabolic health.

the combination of aerobic exercise with resistance training is more effective at reducing fat mass and improving cardiometabolic risk factors in people with the metabolic syndrome compared to aerobic training alone.
